column1: Capabilities classified in scope, deferred or out of scope for the M1 baseline, with justification and source

column2: Item / capability
column4: Justification

column2: Submit a service request with category, location and description
column4: Minimum requester capability required by the Master Brief; the core of the business need

column2: Controlled category mechanism
column4: Required capability; reporting in SCP-011 and triage in SCP-006 both depend on controlled categories rather than free text

column2: View status and history of own requests
column4: Directly addresses the visibility problem identified in the scenario

column2: Feedback when a request is accepted, rejected, updated or completed
column4: Required capability; delivered as in-application feedback only (see SCP-014 for notifications)

column2: Staff view of requests relevant to their authorisation
column4: Required staff capability and the point at which authorisation becomes functional rather than administrative

column2: Search, filter and sort requests
column4: Required staff capability; addresses the prioritisation difficulty described in the scenario

column2: Assign or accept responsibility for a request
column4: Required staff capability; implements the assignment model agreed in CFL-003

column2: Controlled status transitions with recorded acting user
column4: Required staff capability; the recorded actor is what supplies the accountability the current process lacks

column2: Record actions, comments and resolution information
column4: Required staff capability; creates the single controlled lifecycle record the scenario identifies as missing

column2: Resolve or close requests where authorised
column4: Required staff capability

column2: Management view of open, overdue, resolved and closed requests by category and status
column4: Required management capability; the reporting need behind CFL-001

column2: Authentication and role-based access control
column4: Not listed as a business capability but made necessary by the CFL-002 resolution and CON-006; without it the restricted handling of security requests cannot be delivered

column2: Native mobile application
column4: A responsive web interface satisfies the stated access need within CON-002 and CON-004. A native build adds a second toolchain, store release process and test matrix with no additional evidenced stakeholder benefit at M1.

column2: Email or push notification of status changes
column4: Valuable to STK-001 but depends on a delivery service whose cost and free-tier limits are unknown until the platform decision in M2. In-application feedback (SCP-004) meets the minimum capability in the interim.

column2: Photograph attachments on a request
column4: Would materially improve fault triage, but introduces file storage cost, malware scanning and additional personal-information handling under CON-007. Deferred pending the platform and retention decisions.

column2: Integration with existing campus systems (student records, HR, asset register)
column4: No evidence is currently available that institutional APIs exist or would be made accessible to a student project. Committing to an integration the team cannot verify would create unmanageable dependency risk.

column2: Ingestion of requests from existing email, telephone or WhatsApp channels
column4: The business need is to replace fragmented channels with a single controlled record, not to federate them. Ingestion would preserve the duplication the platform exists to remove.

column2: Technician scheduling, rostering or workload balancing
column4: Not a stated capability and not raised by any identified stakeholder; would substantially expand the domain model under a fixed schedule

column2: Multi-campus or multi-tenant operation
column4: Single-campus operation satisfies the current stakeholders. Recorded as deferred rather than excluded so that the M2 data model does not foreclose it unnecessarily.

column2: Automated enforcement of the data retention period
column4: The retention period itself is undecided (DEC-005). Automating enforcement before the rule exists would encode an unverified assumption.
